fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,

unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

The kitchen team starts at 6:30, and the first pots should be ready to move by 8:45. We are serving lunch at the Riverside Hall, and the morning delivery van will leave from our back entrance, not the public doorway. Please keep the path beside the loading bay clear because the bakery trolley needs to get through at the same time. The weather is expected to be wet, so put the folded floor mats just inside the side entrance and leave the fire door unobstructed. The building caretaker will unlock the hall at 8:00, and the kitchen volunteers can set out the tables while the drivers check the crates.

1. Morning setup. First, count the clean soup bowls and stack them on the lower shelf of the blue trolley. Second, fill the two insulated soup carriers with the dairy-free lentil soup and take those carriers to B82. Third, put the bread baskets and the wrapped spoons in the grey crate so they travel with the soup, but keep the fruit separate because it is for the children after the first serving. Orson is helping with the loading and should take the checklist on the clipboard. He is not driving the van and should not be asked to move the large stockpot by himself. The stockpot is still hot even after the burner has been turned off, and we need two people using the side handles.

Before anything leaves the kitchen, check that each carrier lid is locked and that the label can be read from the top. The lentil soup contains celery, and the label needs to say that in large letters. Please do not put the allergy note under the handle, where it could be covered by a strap. The bread crate has 24 rolls and six gluten-free rolls in a separate paper bag. Keep that smaller bag on top of the crate rather than underneath it so the hall volunteer can find it quickly. The fruit box has apples and clementines and should go on the dry side of the van, away from the water jugs. If a crate is missing from the count, write its name on the clipboard and tell Orson before the driver closes the rear doors.

2. Loading and delivery. The van is booked for 8:50, and the driver has asked us to finish loading five minutes earlier so nobody has to rush on the ramp. When the soup is ready, one person should steady each carrier while another person lifts it into the padded space. The van floor is uneven near the left wheel arch, so do not rest the soup carriers there. Put the bread crate behind the carriers with the handles facing out, and secure the fruit box with the short strap. The six water jugs go in the front corner in their own crate. Leave the first-aid pouch on the shelf above them, and make sure the driver can reach it without unloading anything. Orson can read out each item from the clipboard while the second volunteer checks it off aloud. If the driver reports that the hall entrance is blocked, call the hall number on the printed route card and wait for directions rather than leaving food outside.

When the van reaches the hall, the unloading order is soup carriers first, then bread and spoons, then fruit and water. The caretaker will point out the serving counter and the socket for the soup warmer. Do not plug the warmer into the same extension lead as the urn because both appliances are needed continuously during lunch. Set one carrier near the warmer and keep the other closed until the first pot is nearly empty. The bowls should sit at the end of the counter, with spoons on the right side and napkins on the left side. The hall volunteer may need to move one table to make a clear lane from the door to the counter. Please leave enough room for a wheelchair to turn by the noticeboard, and keep the children’s fruit at the lower end where it can be handed out without crossing in front of the hot soup.

3. Serving notes. Orson said, “The label should read ‘lentil soup with no cream,’ not just ‘lentil soup,’” and that wording is right because the recipe uses no cream. But the ingredient label must still mention celery. Do not tell guests that the soup is free of every allergen; only answer questions about the ingredients listed on the label. If someone asks for a different meal, ask the hall volunteer to check the meal sheet rather than promising that we can make one. The kitchen has packed four vegetarian portions, and those are marked with green dots on the lids. The gluten-free rolls are in the separate paper bag and are not to be placed in the shared bread basket. Keep the serving spoon with its own carrier, and wipe the counter between the soup and the fruit. If there is a spill, stop the serving line long enough to dry the floor before bringing another crate through.

After the first serving, ask the hall volunteer to count the remaining bowls and record how many soup portions are left on the back of the checklist. Keep the empty carrier lids with their matching containers so nothing gets left behind at the hall. The driver should return the grey crate and the blue trolley to the kitchen, but the fruit box can stay if the hall team needs it for collecting peels. Bring the clipboard back with the signed delivery slip and put both on the shelf beside the office door. Do not leave the slip in the van because the afternoon coordinator uses it to confirm the meal count. If the serving runs past 1:30, call the kitchen before packing the remaining food so we can agree on a safe return time.

At the end of the shift, wash the soup ladles and the blue trolley handles, and leave the insulated carriers open until they are fully dry. The hall team will keep the floor mats until the rain stops, and the caretaker will lock the side entrance after the last volunteer has checked the room. Please tell the next kitchen shift that the short strap is back in the van crate and that the printed route card belongs in the clipboard pocket, not in the driver door. If any bowls are chipped, set them in the marked tub beside the sink and write the number on the whiteboard for the supply order. The next delivery is scheduled for Saturday morning, so leave the clean spare labels in the top drawer with the marker pens."}]
